Topic: The Essence of Abstract Vector Spaces

Target audience: Undergraduate University Students (Mathematics/Engineering)

Section: section_1 — From Concrete Arrows to Abstract Rules

Lecture lines:
Vectors start as arrows with magnitude and direction.
We now focus on how they behave under operations.
Think of these as abstract objects in a set.
They follow specific rules, regardless of their appearance.
[Asset: Abstract_Transformation_Animation]

Planned animations:
Draw 2D vector using color #FF5733.
Animate vector transformation into a point using color #33FF57.
Overlay labels 'V' for space and 'x' for point.

Section: section_2 — The 8 Axioms: The 'Rulebook' of the Space

Lecture lines:
A Vector Space requires two operations: addition and scaling.
These must satisfy eight fundamental axioms.
Think of these as the laws of physics.

Planned animations:
Display list of 8 axioms in color #FFFF00.
Highlight the 'Additive Identity' axiom with color #FF33FF.
Animate text expansion for clarity.

Section: section_3 — Beyond Arrows: Function Spaces

Lecture lines:
Functions like polynomials can also be vectors.
Summing two functions yields another function.
This expands our horizon beyond physical geometry.

Planned animations:
Show curve with color #00FFFF.
Animate function 'f(x)' mapping to output value.
Label axes 'Input Space' and 'Function Values'.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing Closure: The Gatekeeper

Lecture lines:
Closure is our most important filter.
Operations must keep elements within the space.
[Asset: Gatekeeper_Fence_Animation]

Planned animations:
Visualise vector addition using color #FFA500.
Show resultant vector within same boundary in color #00FF00.
Highlight 'Closure' property tag in bold.

Section: section_5 — Synthesis and Summary

Lecture lines:
Abstract spaces allow structured linear combinations.
This unifies arrows, matrices, and functions.
It powers data science and modern physics.

Planned animations:
Display core formula f(v) = c*v.
Flash formula elements in sequence color #FFFFFF.
Highlight link between prerequisites and final result.

class TeachingScene(Scene):

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]

        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Summary", [
            "Abstract spaces allow structured linear combinations.", 
            "This unifies arrows, matrices, and functions.",

        # Flash elements

        self.wait(1)

        self.lecture[2].set_color("#9999FF")
        # Highlight link
        self.play(Indicate(formula, color="#FFFF99"))
        self.wait(2)
